boundary_rationale: This unit opens the book with the title-and-provenance formula, דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן חִלְקִיָּ֑הוּ מִן הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּעֲנָת֔וֹת בְּאֶ֖רֶץ בִּנְיָמִֽן (oshb:Jer.1.1, byte tier), rendered “The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin” (web:Jer.1.1). The heading then dates the prophet’s word-ministry across a three-reign span — Josiah’s thirteenth year (web:Jer.1.2) through the eleventh year of Zedekiah and Jerusalem’s captivity in the fifth month (web:Jer.1.3) — before any narrative word-event formula appears; the vayehi devar-YHWH onset that opens the call narrative sits at Jer.1.4 (oshb:Jer.1.4), outside this span, so this unit stops at the heading’s own close.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through the call narrative was considered and rejected: the dated title-and-provenance heading and the narrative vayehi devar-YHWH formula belong to structurally distinct device classes.

boundary_rationale: A fresh scene opens with the narrative word-event formula, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.1.4, byte tier) — “Now Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Jer.1.4) — the first of the vayehi devar-YHWH onsets that structure the book’s frame spine. The dialogue that follows (the appointment as a prophet, the touched mouth, the commissioning “Behold, I have today set you over the nations and over the kingdoms, to uproot and to tear down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant” (web:Jer.1.10)) stays inside one unit with its opening formula, since the speaker and addressee do not change across the exchange; a fresh word-event onset instead marks the boundary at Jer.1.11 (oshb:Jer.1.11), where the next vision report opens.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this unit at Jeremiah's protest in web:Jer.1.6 (“Ah, Lord Yahweh”) was considered and rejected, since the protest and Yahweh's answer are turns inside the same call dialogue rather than a fresh scene or addressee.

device_notes: A setumah at Jer.1.3 (single-witness, tier-3) closes the heading just before this span opens; interior petuchah breaks fall after Jer.1.6 and after Jer.1.10 (single-witness, tier-3), the latter aligning with this unit’s own close. A ketiv/qere pair, אצורך אֶצָּרְךָ֤ (oshb:Jer.1.5, byte tier; single-witness), stands behind the appointment clause this unit argues at MT 1:5. The reassurance “to rescue you” (web:Jer.1.8) recurs in close wording at the charge’s own close (web:Jer.1.19): the byte-identical three-word core כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י (oshb:Jer.1.8, byte tier) stands at 4 verses book-wide at byte tier, though the rescue infinitive differs in spelling between the two sites, defective לְהַצִּלֶ֖ךָ (oshb:Jer.1.8) against plene לְהַצִּילֶֽךָ (oshb:Jer.1.19) — a rescue-formula bracket around the call and both vision reports that follow it, even though this unit and the vision reports are kept as separate rows here.

boundary_rationale: A second word-event formula opens a vision report: וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֣י לֵאמֹ֔ר מָה אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ וָאֹמַ֕ר מַקֵּ֥ל שָׁקֵ֖ד אֲנִ֥י רֹאֶֽה (oshb:Jer.1.11, byte tier) — Moreover Yahweh’s word came to me, saying, “Jeremiah, what do you see?” I said, “I see a branch of an almond tree.” (web:Jer.1.11). Yahweh’s reply plays on the answer’s sound: כִּֽי שֹׁקֵ֥ד אֲנִ֛י (oshb:Jer.1.12, byte tier) — Then Yahweh said to me, “You have seen well; for I watch over my word to perform it.” (web:Jer.1.12) — pairing shaqed (almond) with shoqed (watching). The unit closes with that wordplay; a third word-event formula, explicitly marked as recurring a second time, opens the next vision at Jer.1.13 (oshb:Jer.1.13).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this vision into the call narrative that precedes it was considered and rejected, since its own word-event formula (oshb:Jer.1.11) reopens the frame spine rather than continuing web:Jer.1.10's commission without a break.

boundary_rationale: The formula recurs with an explicit ordinal marker: וַיְהִ֨י דְבַר יְהוָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ שֵׁנִ֣ית לֵאמֹ֔ר מָ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה רֹאֶ֑ה וָאֹמַ֗ר סִ֤יר נָפ֨וּחַ֙ אֲנִ֣י רֹאֶ֔ה וּפָנָ֖יו מִפְּנֵ֥י צָפֽוֹנָה (oshb:Jer.1.13, byte tier) — Yahweh’s word came to me the second time, saying, “What do you see?” I said, “I see a boiling cauldron; and it is tipping away from the north.” (web:Jer.1.13). strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting between the vision proper (web:Jer.1.13) and its interpretation (web:Jer.1.14-16) was considered and rejected: the interpretation introduces neither a formula, an imperative, nor a fresh addressee of its own, so it reads as the same speech continuing rather than a fresh unit.

boundary_rationale: A direct charge to the prophet opens with an imperative construction: וְאַתָּה֙ תֶּאְזֹ֣ר מָתְנֶ֔יךָ (oshb:Jer.1.17, byte tier) — “You therefore put your belt on your waist” (web:Jer.1.17) — turning from the vision report's content back to second-person address of Jeremiah himself, echoing the don't-be-afraid charge of web:Jer.1.8. boundary_rationale: Chapter 2 opens with its own word-event formula, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.2.1, byte tier) — “Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Jer.2.1) — the go-and-proclaim pair introducing the messenger formula and the quoted divine speech: הָלֹ֡ךְ וְקָֽרָאתָ֩ בְאָזְנֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה זָכַ֤רְתִּי לָךְ֙ חֶ֣סֶד נְעוּרַ֔יִךְ אַהֲבַ֖ת כְּלוּלֹתָ֑יִךְ (oshb:Jer.2.2, byte tier) — “Go and proclaim in the ears of Jerusalem, saying” the messenger formula, then “I remember for you the kindness of your youth, your love as a bride” (web:Jer.2.2). boundary_rationale: An attend-the-word imperative addressed to the whole house of Israel opens the covenant lawsuit proper: שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְכָֽל מִשְׁפְּח֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.2.4, byte tier) — “Hear Yahweh’s word, O house of Jacob, and all the families of the house of Israel!” (web:Jer.2.4). The unit runs the formal rib pattern through to its evidentiary close: the fathers’ baseless complaint (web:Jer.2.5), the wilderness rehearsal (web:Jer.2.6-7), the priests’/prophets’ failure (web:Jer.2.8), the renewed contention announcement at web:Jer.2.9, the coastland witnesses (web:Jer.2.10), the astonished-heavens summons (web:Jer.2.12), and the twin-evil indictment closing at web:Jer.2.13. A messenger formula stands verse-initially at כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.2.5, byte tier), relayed in the same divine mouth with no change of frame-owner, and imperative chains stand at עִבְר֞וּ אִיֵּ֤י כִתִּיִּים֙ וּרְא֔וּ וְקֵדָ֛ר שִׁלְח֥וּ וְהִֽתְבּוֹנְנ֖וּ (oshb:Jer.2.10, byte tier) and שֹׁ֥מּוּ שָׁמַ֖יִם עַל זֹ֑את וְשַׂעֲר֛וּ חָרְב֥וּ (oshb:Jer.2.12, byte tier); both sound as the lawsuit's own witness-summons device rather than opening a fresh discourse frame. No fresh word-event formula intervenes before Jer.2.14, where a rhetorical-question series shifts the argument's shape.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through the rhetorical questions of web:Jer.2.14ff was considered and rejected: those verses lack a witness summons or verdict language of the rib pattern's own kind, so the formal lawsuit is read as closing at its own evidentiary close in web:Jer.2.13.

boundary_rationale: The argument shifts from formal lawsuit to a sustained run of rhetorical questions: הַעֶ֨בֶד֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִם יְלִ֥יד בַּ֖יִת ה֑וּא מַדּ֖וּעַ הָיָ֥ה לָבַֽז (oshb:Jer.2.14, byte tier) — “Is Israel a slave? Is he born into slavery? Why has he become a captive?” (web:Jer.2.14). Inside the span, no word-event formula and no messenger formula stand at all; imperative forms appear at MT 2:19, 2:23 and 2:25, but as content commands inside the continuing address rather than fresh discourse frames; participant shifts stand at MT 2:28, turning to a masculine-singular vocative naming Judah at וְאַיֵּ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֣יתָ ... יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.2.28, byte tier), coinciding with the setumah disclosed inside this span, and at MT 2:29, turning to the plural at כֻּלְּכֶ֛ם פְּשַׁעְתֶּ֥ם בִּ֖י נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.2.29, byte tier); neither is adopted as an internal cut here. The indictment moves through the vine (web:Jer.2.21), dromedary and donkey (web:Jer.2.23-24), and idol-futility (web:Jer.2.27-28) metaphors; the unit is held together as one span rather than cut at those metaphor changes, which mark topic, not formula. It closes “Your own sword has devoured your prophets” (web:Jer.2.30); an attend-the-word imperative opens the next unit at Jer.2.31 (oshb:Jer.2.31).

A participant-shift rival was also weighed at MT 2:28 / MT 2:29 — the turn to a masculine-singular vocative naming Judah at וְאַיֵּ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֣יתָ ... יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.2.28, byte tier), the first coinciding with the setumah inside this span, and then to the plural at כֻּלְּכֶ֛ם פְּשַׁעְתֶּ֥ם בִּ֖י נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.2.29, byte tier), the second closing on its own neum-YHWH formula — but it was not adopted, since no tier-1 onset accompanies either turn to carry a fresh unit by itself.

We will come to you no more’?” (web:Jer.2.31), pairing a see-imperative with the word-of-Yahweh as its object, רְא֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.2.31, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier), the same imperative-plus-object discourse-frame shape as שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.2.4, byte tier; sweep: 10 verses, skeleton tier). boundary_rationale: A case-law analogy opens the chapter: “They say, ‘If a man puts away his wife, and she goes from him, and becomes another man’s, should he return to her again?” (web:Jer.3.1). The verse opens on a bound, dependent infinitive with no governing verb of its own, לֵאמֹ֡ר (oshb:Jer.3.1, byte tier), sitting exactly at the seam and signaling dependence on what precedes rather than supplying a formula of this unit's own; the onset warrant instead rests on the analogy's topic shift. The analogy turns to direct application at the same verse’s close: וְאַ֗תְּ זָנִית֙ רֵעִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים וְשׁ֥וֹב אֵלַ֖י נְאֻם יְהֹוָֽה (oshb:Jer.3.1, byte tier) — “But you have played the prostitute with many lovers; yet return again to me” (web:Jer.3.1). A closure-shaped formula, נְאֻם יְהֹוָֽה (oshb:Jer.3.1, byte tier), stands at the end of this same opening verse, mid-span rather than at this unit's own close five verses later. The contiguous consonantal run of this plene spelling, shuv, stands at 41 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, the earliest of those 41 at Jer.3.1; the broader return root inflects earlier still, in its own attested spellings at וּמְשֻֽׁבוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ (oshb:Jer.2.19), יְשִׁיבֶ֑נָּה (oshb:Jer.2.24) and שָׁ֥ב אַפּ֖וֹ (oshb:Jer.2.35). The address continues through the bare-heights imagery (web:Jer.3.2) and the withheld-rain consequence (web:Jer.3.3) to a quoted plea at web:Jer.3.4-5. boundary_rationale: “The word which came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying” (web:Jer.18.1) opens הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.18.1, byte tier) -- the hadavar-asher-hayah-el-Yirmeyahu shape that opens this frame. The command “Arise, and go down to the potter’s house” (web:Jer.18.2), ק֥וּם וְיָרַדְתָּ֖ בֵּ֣ית הַיּוֹצֵ֑ר וְשָׁ֖מָּה אַשְׁמִֽיעֲךָ֥ אֶת דְּבָרָֽי (oshb:Jer.18.2, byte tier), and the performance “Then I went down to the potter’s house” (web:Jer.18.3), וָאֵרֵ֖ד בֵּ֣ית הַיּוֹצֵ֑ר (oshb:Jer.18.3, byte tier; the same verse carries a ketiv/qere note on its own 'behold' clause just after, consulted and not spliced through), lead into a second, internal word-event, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֽוֹר (oshb:Jer.18.5, byte tier), and Yahweh's interpretation, “House of Israel, can’t I do with you as this potter?” (web:Jer.18.6), הֲכַיּוֹצֵ֨ר הַזֶּ֜ה לֹא אוּכַ֨ל לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לָכֶ֛ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Jer.18.6, byte tier), the same verse closing on the plain article-bearing noun, בְּיַ֣ד הַיּוֹצֵ֔ר (oshb:Jer.18.6, byte tier). The application to Judah by name, “Behold, I frame evil against you” (web:Jer.18.11), turns the same consonantal root into a verb rather than repeating the noun: הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י יוֹצֵ֤ר עֲלֵיכֶם֙ רָעָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier) is a bare participle, byte-distinct from the article-bearing noun that names the craftsman at 18:2, 18:3, 18:4 and 18:6 (sweep: 5 verses on the article-bearing form); the shared object is the consonantal root itself, which recurs at the wider, article-free search across the book (sweep: 10 verses on the bare root). That shared root, not a repeated token, binds the application and the people's own refusal, “It is in vain” (web:Jer.18.12), נוֹאָ֑שׁ (oshb:Jer.18.12, byte tier), to the observed sign. The join that follows changes neither the divine mouth nor, until mid-verse, the addressee: the instruction “Ask now among the nations” (web:Jer.18.13), שַֽׁאֲלוּ נָא֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier), repeats the same second-person-plural imperative-plus-entreaty shape already commanding Judah two verses earlier, שׁ֣וּבוּ נָ֗א (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier); its own formula, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier), is subordinated to the back-linking לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier) rather than opening a fresh frame -- the identical formula, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier), already stands inside the command to speak at 18:11, so the same mouth carries both sides of the join. Third-person description does not begin until mid-verse: “The virgin of Israel has done a very horrible thing” (web:Jer.18.13), שַֽׁעֲרֻרִת֙ עָשְׂתָ֣ה מְאֹ֔ד בְּתוּלַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier), and the material runs through the snow-of-Lebanon comparison and the forgotten-paths charge to the sentence “I will scatter them as with an east wind before the enemy” (web:Jer.18.17), כְּרֽוּחַ קָדִ֥ים אֲפִיצֵ֖ם לִפְנֵ֣י אוֹיֵ֑ב (oshb:Jer.18.17, byte tier), the divine answer the 'therefore' of 18:13 supplies to that refusal, keeping command, performance, interpretation, application, and reply one enacted-sign row.

boundary_rationale: A fresh command opens the row: “Go, and buy a potter’s earthen container, and take some of the elders of the people and of the elders of the priests” (web:Jer.19.1), spliced כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הָל֛וֹךְ וְקָנִ֥יתָ (oshb:Jer.19.1, byte tier) — the messenger formula followed by an infinitive absolute and a waw-prefixed second-person-singular suffix-conjugation form, not an imperative, opening on the prophet as addressee and distinct from the potter-house visit that precedes it and from the prophet’s own petition just before it, building a new commissioned sign on a jar rather than clay on a wheel. Therefore I have drawn you with loving kindness.” (web:Jer.31.3). Rebuilding imagery follows, ע֤וֹד אֶבְנֵךְ֙ וְֽנִבְנֵ֔ית בְּתוּלַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ע֚וֹד תַּעְדִּ֣י תֻפַּ֔יִךְ וְיָצָ֖את בִּמְח֥וֹל מְשַׂחֲקִֽים (oshb:Jer.31.4, byte), matching “I will build you again, and you will be built, O virgin of Israel. You will again be adorned with your tambourines, and will go out in the dances of those who make merry.” (web:Jer.31.4) — virgin Israel, tambourines, dances. It closes on a quoted summons, כִּ֣י יֶשׁ י֔וֹם קָרְא֥וּ נֹצְרִ֖ים בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם ק֚וּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה צִיּ֔וֹן אֶל יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ (oshb:Jer.31.6, byte), matching “For there will be a day that the watchmen on the hills of Ephraim cry, ‘Arise! Let’s go up to Zion to Yahweh our God.’” (web:Jer.31.6). A fresh koh-amar opens a jubilant call to sing at verse 7, and this row stops there.

boundary_rationale: Yahweh's own word-event formula opens the response to the burning, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ אַחֲרֵ֣י שְׂרֹ֣ף הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.36.27, byte), matching “Then Yahweh's word came to Jeremiah, after the king had burned” (web:Jer.36.27) A paseq falls at this same verse. The command to rewrite follows without a break (web:Jer.36.28), and a pronouncement naming Jehoiakim specifically opens on its own koh-amar, וְעַל יְהוֹיָקִ֤ים מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ תֹּאמַ֔ר כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.36.29, byte), matching “Concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say, 'Yahweh says: "You” (web:Jer.36.29) charging him with burning the very scroll that warned of Babylon's coming -- a setumah falls at this same opening verse. A second koh-amar carries the sentence itself, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה עַל יְהֽוֹיָקִים֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה לֹא יִֽהְיֶה לּ֥וֹ יוֹשֵׁ֖ב עַל כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֑ד (oshb:Jer.36.30, byte), matching “Therefore Yahweh says concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: "He will have no one to sit on David's throne.” (web:Jer.36.30) -- no heir on David's throne, his own body cast out. The punishment then extends to his offspring, his servants, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem and Judah, closing on their own failure to listen (וּפָקַדְתִּ֨י עָלָ֧יו וְעַל זַרְע֛וֹ וְעַל עֲבָדָ֖יו אֶת עֲוֺנָ֑ם וְהֵבֵאתִ֣י עֲ֠לֵיהֶם וְעַל יֹשְׁבֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם וְאֶל אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֗ה אֵ֧ת כָּל הָרָעָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א שָׁמֵֽעוּ (oshb:Jer.36.31, byte), matching “I will punish him, his offspring, and his servants for their iniquity. I will bring on them, on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and on the men of Judah, all the evil that I have pronounced against them, but they didn't listen.” (web:Jer.36.31)); a setumah falls at this closing verse too. The chapter and the row close on Jeremiah's own replacement of the scroll, וְיִרְמְיָ֜הוּ לָקַ֣ח מְגִלָּ֣ה אַחֶ֗רֶת וַֽיִּתְּנָהּ֮ אֶל בָּר֣וּךְ בֶּן נֵרִיָּהוּ֮ הַסֹּפֵר֒ וַיִּכְתֹּ֤ב עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ מִפִּ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.36.32, byte), matching “Then Jeremiah took another scroll, and gave it to Baruch the scribe, the son of Neriah, who wrote therein from the mouth of Jeremiah” (web:Jer.36.32) continuing, וְע֨וֹד נוֹסַ֧ף עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם דְּבָרִ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים כָּהֵֽמָּה (oshb:Jer.36.32, byte), matching “and many similar words were added to them.” (web:Jer.36.32) A further setumah closes this same verse.

boundary_rationale: The span opens the part on a reign-change notice, וַיִּ֨מְלָךְ מֶ֔לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בֶּן יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ תַּ֗חַת כָּנְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן יְה֣וֹיָקִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִמְלִ֛יךְ נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל בְּאֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.37.1, byte), matching “Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned as king instead of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.” (web:Jer.37.1) — the bytes name the new king’s predecessor כָּנְיָ֨הוּ֙ (Konyahu, byte; oshb:Jer.37.1), the Coniah form, one of three name forms this king carries across the book (sweep: 3 verses); the reign's installer carries no further identification beyond the royal title, “whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king” (web:Jer.37.1), the resh-family spelling נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר standing in the same clause (oshb:Jer.37.1, byte). Verse 2 continues the same notice with a general character report, וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֛ע ה֥וּא וַעֲבָדָ֖יו וְעַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ אֶל דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִֽיא (oshb:Jer.37.2, byte), matching “But neither he, nor his servants, nor the people of the land, listened to Yahweh's words, which he spoke by the prophet Jeremiah.” (web:Jer.37.2) — naming the king, his servants, and the people of the land together, a summary claim about the reign rather than a dated scene. The inventory’s own setumah sits at oshb:Jer.36.32 (single-witness WLC archival, weak, tier-3 corroboration, governed by the Prophets addendum), immediately before this span’s own front seam; no mark falls inside verses 1-2 themselves.

boundary_rationale: A named embassy opens the scene, matching “Zedekiah the king sent Jehucal the son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah, the priest, to the prophet Jeremiah, saying,” (web:Jer.37.3), asking him to pray to Yahweh their God on their behalf — Zedekiah sending two officials to ask Jeremiah to pray; a petuchah closes this opening notice at oshb:Jer.37.5 (single-witness WLC; Prophets tier-3, weak corroboration), keying the junction immediately before the oracle's own onset, the notice that Pharaoh's army had left Egypt, וְחֵ֥יל פַּרְעֹ֖ה יָצָ֣א מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַיִּשְׁמְע֨וּ הַכַּשְׂדִּ֜ים הַצָּרִ֤ים עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ אֶת שִׁמְעָ֔ם וַיֵּ֣עָל֔וּ מֵעַ֖ל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Jer.37.5, byte). boundary_rationale: A new set of four named officials opens the span, וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע שְׁפַטְיָ֣ה בֶן מַתָּ֗ן וּגְדַלְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן פַּשְׁח֔וּר וְיוּכַל֙ בֶּן שֶׁ֣לֶמְיָ֔הוּ וּפַשְׁח֖וּר בֶּן מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה אֶ֨ת הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ מְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל כָּל הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte), matching “Shephatiah the son of Mattan, Gedaliah the son of Pashhur, Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur the son of Malchijah heard the words that Jeremiah spoke to all the people, saying,” (web:Jer.38.1); a setumah marks this same verse, oshb:Jer.38.1 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration). boundary_rationale: A setumah closes oshb:Jer.45.5 in the parashah inventory (WLC's single witness ranks it tier-3 and weak under the Prophets-addendum ruling). That mark falls immediately before this unit's own opening on the nations-rubric that stands over the whole collection, אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֧ה דְבַר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא עַל הַגּוֹיִֽם (oshb:Jer.46.1, byte), matching “Yahweh’s word which came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.” (web:Jer.46.1) — one of only four verses in the book carrying this exact asher-hayah debar-YHWH el-Yirmeyahu shape (sweep: 4 verses), naming Jeremiah before naming any single nation. Egypt's own header follows at once with its date folded inside the same verse, לְמִצְרַ֗יִם עַל חֵ֨יל פַּרְעֹ֤ה נְכוֹ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֥ה עַל נְהַר פְּרָ֖ת בְּכַרְכְּמִ֑שׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִכָּ֗ה נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל בִּשְׁנַת֙ הָֽרְבִיעִ֔ית לִיהוֹיָקִ֥ים בֶּן יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.46.2, byte), matching “Of Egypt: concerning the army of Pharaoh Necoh king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates in Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah.” (web:Jer.46.2) — Pharaoh Necoh, the Euphrates, Carchemish, and Nebuchadnezzar (spelled here נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙, the resh-family form) are all named before the battle-vision itself begins, and the fourth-year date sits header-internal rather than verse-initial. The battle-summons opens directly on the next verse with no intervening narration, עִרְכ֤וּ מָגֵן֙ וְצִנָּ֔ה וּגְשׁ֖וּ לַמִּלְחָמָֽה (oshb:Jer.46.3, byte), matching “Prepare the buckler and shield, and draw near to battle!” (web:Jer.46.3), continuing אִסְר֣וּ הַסּוּסִ֗ים וַֽעֲלוּ֙ הַפָּ֣רָשִׁ֔ים וְהִֽתְיַצְּב֖וּ בְּכ֥וֹבָעִ֑ים מִרְקוּ֙ הָֽרְמָחִ֔ים לִבְשׁ֖וּ הַסִּרְיֹנֹֽת (oshb:Jer.46.4, byte), matching “Harness the horses, and get up, you horsemen, and stand up with your helmets. Polish the spears, put on the coats of mail.” (web:Jer.46.4) — imperatives addressed to unnamed combatants, not yet a named vocative. Shock at the rout follows, מַדּ֣וּעַ רָאִ֗יתִי הֵ֣מָּה חַתִּים֮ נְסֹגִ֣ים אָחוֹר֒ וְגִבּוֹרֵיהֶ֣ם יֻכַּ֔תּוּ וּמָנ֥וֹס נָ֖סוּ וְלֹ֣א הִפְנ֑וּ מָג֥וֹר מִסָּבִ֖יב נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.46.5, byte), matching “Why have I seen it? They are dismayed and are turned backward. Their mighty ones are beaten down, have fled in haste, and don’t look back. Terror is on every side," says Yahweh.” (web:Jer.46.5); the verse closes on neum-YHWH, but no fresh tier-1 onset follows it at the next verse, so the formula corroborates rather than closes a unit here, and the flight continues without a break, אַל יָנ֣וּס הַקַּ֔ל וְאַל יִמָּלֵ֖ט הַגִּבּ֑וֹר צָפ֨וֹנָה֙ עַל יַ֣ד נְהַר פְּרָ֔ת כָּשְׁל֖וּ וְנָפָֽלוּ (oshb:Jer.46.6, byte), matching “Don’t let the swift flee away, nor the mighty man escape. In the north by the river Euphrates they have stumbled and fallen.” (web:Jer.46.6). A rhetorical question turns the description toward an extended Nile-simile, מִי זֶ֖ה כַּיְאֹ֣ר יַֽעֲלֶ֑ה כַּנְּהָר֕וֹת יִֽתְגָּעֲשׁ֖וּ מֵימָֽיו (oshb:Jer.46.7, byte), matching “Who is this who rises up like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge?” (web:Jer.46.7), and Egypt's own boast is quoted inside the same figure, מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ כַּיְאֹ֣ר יַֽעֲלֶ֔ה וְכַנְּהָר֖וֹת יִתְגֹּ֣עֲשׁוּ מָ֑יִם וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַֽעֲלֶה֙ אֲכַסֶּה אֶ֔רֶץ אֹבִ֥ידָה עִ֖יר וְיֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ (oshb:Jer.46.8, byte), matching “Egypt rises up like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge. He says, ‘I will rise up. I will cover the earth. I will destroy cities and its inhabitants.’” (web:Jer.46.8). A summons to the allied troops follows, עֲל֤וּ הַסּוּסִים֙ וְהִתְהֹלְל֣וּ הָרֶ֔כֶב וְיֵצְא֖וּ הַגִּבּוֹרִ֑ים כּ֤וּשׁ וּפוּט֙ תֹּפְשֵׂ֣י מָגֵ֔ן וְלוּדִ֕ים תֹּפְשֵׂ֖י דֹּ֥רְכֵי קָֽשֶׁת (oshb:Jer.46.9, byte), matching “Go up, you horses! Rage, you chariots! Let the mighty men go out: Cush and Put, who handle the shield; and the Ludim, who handle and bend the bow.” (web:Jer.46.9), and the scene is given its theological frame, וְֽהַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא לַאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת י֤וֹם נְקָמָה֙ לְהִנָּקֵ֣ם מִצָּרָ֔יו וְאָכְלָ֥ה חֶ֨רֶב֙ וְשָׂ֣בְעָ֔ה וְרָוְתָ֖ה מִדָּמָ֑ם כִּ֣י זֶ֠בַח לַאדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת בְּאֶ֥רֶץ צָפ֖וֹן אֶל נְהַר פְּרָֽת (oshb:Jer.46.10, byte), matching “For that day is of the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge himself of his adversaries. The sword will devour and be satiated, and will drink its fill of their blood; for the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, has a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates.” (web:Jer.46.10) — the construction לַאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת is quoted here at the byte tier as its own prefixed token object, standing at two verses book-wide and recurring a second time later in this same verse (sweep: 2 verses). The first of the vision's three direct addresses to name its addressee falls next, עֲלִ֤י גִלְעָד֙ וּקְחִ֣י צֳרִ֔י בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם לַשָּׁוְא֙ הרביתי הִרְבֵּ֣ית רְפֻא֔וֹת תְּעָלָ֖ה אֵ֥ין לָֽךְ (oshb:Jer.46.11, byte), matching “Go up into Gilead, and take balm, virgin daughter of Egypt. You use many medicines in vain. There is no healing for you.” (web:Jer.46.11) — a named vocative, בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם, to Egypt personified as a virgin daughter, distinct from the unnamed addressees of the plural imperatives at oshb:Jer.46.3 and oshb:Jer.46.9 (sweep: 3 verses: Jer.46.3, Jer.46.9, Jer.46.11), continuing the same battle-vision rather than opening a new one, and the verse itself carries a ketiv/qere pair, הרביתי written against הִרְבֵּ֣ית read (single-witness). boundary_rationale: The parashah inventory marks oshb:Jer.46.12 with a petuchah (WLC single witness; the Prophets addendum holds this tier-3 and never a driver). That mark falls immediately before this unit's own fresh word-event heading, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הַנָּבִ֑יא לָב֗וֹא נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל לְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם (oshb:Jer.46.13, byte), matching “The word that Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah the prophet, how that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon should come and strike the land of Egypt:” (web:Jer.46.13) — the shape here is built on the verb דִּבֶּ֣ר ("spoke") rather than the verb hayah ("came/was") that underlies all three of the book's canonical word-event shapes, so it is disclosed as its own header device rather than folded into any of them. The heading opens directly onto a fresh summons to proclaim, הַגִּ֤ידוּ בְמִצְרַ֨יִם֙ וְהַשְׁמִ֣יעוּ בְמִגְדּ֔וֹל וְהַשְׁמִ֥יעוּ בְנֹ֖ף וּבְתַחְפַּנְחֵ֑ס אִמְר֗וּ הִתְיַצֵּב֙ וְהָכֵ֣ן לָ֔ךְ כִּֽי אָכְלָ֥ה חֶ֖רֶב סְבִיבֶֽיךָ (oshb:Jer.46.14, byte), matching “Declare in Egypt, publish in Migdol, and publish in Memphis and in Tahpanhes; say, ‘Stand up, and prepare, for the sword has devoured around you.’” (web:Jer.46.14) — imperatives addressed to the frontier garrison towns rather than to Egypt as a single named addressee. A rhetorical question follows without any new frame, מַדּ֖וּעַ נִסְחַ֣ף אַבִּירֶ֑יךָ לֹ֣א עָמַ֔ד כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה הֲדָפֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.46.15, byte), matching “Why are your strong ones swept away? They didn’t stand, because Yahweh pushed them.” (web:Jer.46.15), and the mercenaries' own flight is reported in their own quoted words, הִרְבָּ֖ה כּוֹשֵׁ֑ל גַּם נָפַ֞ל אִ֣ישׁ אֶל רֵעֵ֗הוּ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ ק֣וּמָה וְנָשֻׁ֣בָה אֶל עַמֵּ֗נוּ וְאֶל אֶ֨רֶץ֙ מֽוֹלַדְתֵּ֔נוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י חֶ֥רֶב הַיּוֹנָֽה (oshb:Jer.46.16, byte), matching “He made many to stumble. Yes, they fell on one another. They said, ‘Arise! Let’s go again to our own people, and to the land of our birth, from the oppressing sword.’” (web:Jer.46.16) — this verse likewise carries a paseq, from the single-witness seg-layer tally -- a count, not a position. The crowd's mockery of Pharaoh is quoted next, קָרְא֖וּ שָׁ֑ם פַּרְעֹ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ שָׁא֔וֹן הֶעֱבִ֖יר הַמּוֹעֵֽד (oshb:Jer.46.17, byte), matching “They cried there, ‘Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise; he has let the appointed time pass by.’” (web:Jer.46.17), and the unit closes on a divine oath, חַי אָ֨נִי֙ נְאֻם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ כִּ֚י כְּתָב֣וֹר בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וּכְכַרְמֶ֖ל בַּיָּ֥ם יָבֽוֹא (oshb:Jer.46.18, byte), matching “As I live,” says the King, whose name is Yahweh of Armies, “surely like Tabor among the mountains, and like Carmel by the sea, so he will come. That mark falls immediately before this unit's own lamed-initial header, which carries its divine-speech formula and its own woe cry folded into the same verse, לְמוֹאָ֡ב כֹּֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל ה֤וֹי אֶל נְבוֹ֙ כִּ֣י שֻׁדָּ֔דָה הֹבִ֥ישָׁה נִלְכְּדָ֖ה קִרְיָתָ֑יִם הֹבִ֥ישָׁה הַמִּשְׂגָּ֖ב וָחָֽתָּה (oshb:Jer.48.1, byte), matching “Of Moab. Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Woe to Nebo! For it is laid waste. Kiriathaim is disappointed. It is taken. Misgab is put to shame and broken down.” (web:Jer.48.1) — the same full divine-title stack as יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל, already cited at oshb:Jer.46.25 (sweep: 32 verses), opens the sentence, and the woe sits INSIDE this header verse, over the town of Nebo, rather than as a fresh onset following a header already complete; it is disclosed here as a woe-inside-header-verse shape, distinct from the bare woe-onsets that open other units elsewhere in the book, and the divine-speech formula itself only sets this unit's frame rather than changing an established one. The devastation report continues at once, אֵ֣ין עוֹד֮ תְּהִלַּ֣ת מוֹאָב֒ בְּחֶשְׁבּ֗וֹן חָשְׁב֤וּ עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ רָעָ֔ה לְכ֖וּ וְנַכְרִיתֶ֣נָּה מִגּ֑וֹי גַּם מַדְמֵ֣ן תִּדֹּ֔מִּי אַחֲרַ֖יִךְ תֵּ֥לֶךְ חָֽרֶב (oshb:Jer.48.2, byte), matching “The praise of Moab is no more. In Heshbon they have devised evil against her: ‘Come! Let’s cut her off from being a nation.’ You also, Madmen, will be brought to silence. The sword will pursue you.” (web:Jer.48.2) — a nearby town is addressed directly in passing inside an otherwise third-person catalogue of towns, a brief apostrophe rather than a fresh scene of its own. The catalogue continues, ק֥וֹל צְעָקָ֖ה מֵחֹֽרוֹנָ֑יִם שֹׁ֖ד וָשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּדֽוֹל (oshb:Jer.48.3, byte), matching “The sound of a cry from Horonaim, desolation and great destruction!” (web:Jer.48.3), and נִשְׁבְּרָ֖ה מוֹאָ֑ב הִשְׁמִ֥יעוּ זְּעָקָ֖ה צעוריה צְעִירֶֽיהָ (oshb:Jer.48.4, byte), matching “Moab is destroyed. Her little ones have caused a cry to be heard.” (web:Jer.48.4) — this verse carries a ketiv/qere pair, צעוריה written against צְעִירֶֽיהָ read (single-witness). The report closes its first movement on the roads of Luhith and Horonaim, כִּ֚י מַעֲלֵ֣ה הלחות הַלּוּחִ֔ית בִּבְכִ֖י יַֽעֲלֶה בֶּ֑כִי כִּ֚י בְּמוֹרַ֣ד חוֹרֹנַ֔יִם צָרֵ֥י צַֽעֲקַת שֶׁ֖בֶר שָׁמֵֽעוּ (oshb:Jer.48.5, byte), matching “For they will go up by the ascent of Luhith with continual weeping. For at the descent of Horonaim they have heard the distress of the cry of destruction.” (web:Jer.48.5) — another ketiv/qere pair, הלחות written against הַלּוּחִ֔ית read (single-witness). A fresh imperative opens the next movement without a new named addressee, נֻ֖סוּ מַלְּט֣וּ נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם וְתִֽהְיֶ֕ינָה כַּעֲרוֹעֵ֖ר בַּמִּדְבָּֽר (oshb:Jer.48.6, byte), matching “Flee! Save your lives! Be like the juniper bush in the wilderness.” (web:Jer.48.6), and the indictment of Moab's own trust follows, כִּ֠י יַ֣עַן בִּטְחֵ֤ךְ בְּמַעֲשַׂ֨יִךְ֙ וּבְא֣וֹצְרוֹתַ֔יִךְ גַּם אַ֖תְּ תִּלָּכֵ֑דִי וְיָצָ֤א כמיש כְמוֹשׁ֙ בַּגּוֹלָ֔ה כֹּהֲנָ֥יו וְשָׂרָ֖יו יחד יַחְדָּֽיו (oshb:Jer.48.7, byte), matching “For, because you have trusted in your works and in your treasures, you also will be taken. Chemosh will go out into captivity, his priests and his princes together.” (web:Jer.48.7) — this verse is one of the twelve doubled ketiv/qere sites in the book, carrying two separate pairs: כמיש written against כְמוֹשׁ֙ read (single-witness), and יחד written against יַחְדָּֽיו read (single-witness). The unit closes on a universal declaration, וְיָבֹ֨א שֹׁדֵ֜ד אֶל כָּל עִ֗יר וְעִיר֙ לֹ֣א תִמָּלֵ֔ט וְאָבַ֥ד הָעֵ֖מֶק וְנִשְׁמַ֣ד הַמִּישֹׁ֑ר אֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.48.8, byte), matching “The destroyer will come on every city, and no city will escape; the valley also will perish, and the plain will be destroyed, as Yahweh has spoken.” (web:Jer.48.8). A fresh imperative opens the next verse with a different figure — wings rather than flight on foot — תְּנוּ צִ֣יץ לְמוֹאָ֔ב כִּ֥י נָצֹ֖א תֵּצֵ֑א וְעָרֶ֨יהָ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ינָה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בָּהֵֽן (oshb:Jer.48.9, byte), which reads “Give wings to Moab, that she may fly and get herself away: and her cities will become a desolation, without anyone to dwell in them.” (web:Jer.48.9); this unit does not extend to that verse.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at the flee-imperative partway through, reading it as its own scene against the town-catalogue before it, was considered and rejected: the imperative carries no named vocative addressee of its own, unlike the structural direct addresses elsewhere in this chapter, and the indictment it opens (trust in works and treasures) continues in the same voice through the universal declaration that closes the unit.
literature_type_guess: a lamed-header opening a town-by-town devastation report for Moab
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The woe at the header verse is disclosed as embedded within the header itself, role-split before any digit, distinct from the bare and vav-prefixed woe shapes counted elsewhere in the book; the brief direct address to a nearby town partway through is disclosed as an incidental apostrophe rather than a structural vocative, since the surrounding catalogue stays in the third person on either side of it.

boundary_rationale: A plural imperative opens this unit, תְּנוּ צִ֣יץ לְמוֹאָ֔ב כִּ֥י נָצֹ֖א תֵּצֵ֑א וְעָרֶ֨יהָ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ינָה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בָּהֵֽן (oshb:Jer.48.9, byte), matching “Give wings to Moab, that she may fly and get herself away: and her cities will become a desolation, without anyone to dwell in them.” (web:Jer.48.9) — no vocative addressee is named, but the verse just closed ends on its own verse-final speech attribution, אֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.48.8, byte), a three-token relative-clause divine-speech attribution standing at exactly one verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse); no such closing attribution precedes the plural imperative at oshb:Jer.48.6, so the near-side closure together with this verse's imperative onset marks the seam here rather than there. A twofold curse follows, אָר֗וּר עֹשֶׂ֛ה מְלֶ֥אכֶת יְהוָ֖ה רְמִיָּ֑ה וְאָר֕וּר מֹנֵ֥עַ חַרְבּ֖וֹ מִדָּֽם (oshb:Jer.48.10, byte), matching “Cursed is he who does the work of Yahweh negligently; and cursed is he who keeps back his sword from blood.” (web:Jer.48.10) — the noun רְמִיָּ֑ה ("slackness/negligence"), rendered negligently here, is a consonantal substring of the prophet's own name and is quoted here as a token-bound object attested at exactly one verse at byte and at skeleton tier (oshb:Jer.48.10) (sweep: 1 verse), never as a book-wide count, precisely because a bare consonantal substring sweep for it returns 118 verses and 132 token occurrences, since it matches inside every occurrence of the prophet's own name. The wine-on-the-lees figure for Moab's undisturbed ease opens next, שַׁאֲנַ֨ן מוֹאָ֜ב מִנְּעוּרָ֗יו וְשֹׁקֵ֥ט הוּא֙ אֶל שְׁמָרָ֔יו וְלֹֽא הוּרַ֤ק מִכְּלִי֙ אֶל כֶּ֔לִי וּבַגּוֹלָ֖ה לֹ֣א הָלָ֑ךְ עַל כֵּ֗ן עָמַ֤ד טַעְמוֹ֙ בּ֔וֹ וְרֵיח֖וֹ לֹ֥א נָמָֽר (oshb:Jer.48.11, byte), matching “Moab has been at ease from his youth, and he has settled on his dregs, and has not been emptied from vessel to vessel, neither has he gone into captivity; therefore his taste remains in him, and his scent is not changed.” (web:Jer.48.11). oshb:Jer.48.11 carries its own setumah in the parashah layer, disclosed as WLC single-witness texture, tier-3 weak among the Prophets. That mark is disclosed as texture rather than a sub-boundary, since the very next verse continues the same figure with its own consequence clause. That continuation follows without a break, לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּ֖ה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה וְשִׁלַּחְתִּי ל֥וֹ צֹעִ֖ים וְצֵעֻ֑הוּ וְכֵלָ֣יו יָרִ֔יקוּ וְנִבְלֵיהֶ֖ם יְנַפֵּֽצוּ (oshb:Jer.48.12, byte), matching “Therefore behold, the days come," says Yahweh, "that I will send to him those who pour off, and they will pour him off; and they will empty his vessels, and break their containers in pieces.” (web:Jer.48.12) — the neum-YHWH here sits mid-verse, introducing rather than closing the sentence. The unit closes on a comparison to Israel's own shame at Bethel, וּבֹ֥שׁ מוֹאָ֖ב מִכְּמ֑וֹשׁ כַּאֲשֶׁר בֹּ֨שׁוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִבֵּ֥ית אֵ֖ל מִבְטֶחָֽם (oshb:Jer.48.13, byte), matching “Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, their confidence.” (web:Jer.48.13). A fresh taunting question opens the next verse, אֵ֚יךְ תֹּֽאמְר֔וּ גִּבּוֹרִ֖ים אֲנָ֑חְנוּ וְאַנְשֵׁי חַ֖יִל לַמִּלְחָמָֽה (oshb:Jer.48.14, byte), matching “How do you say, ‘We are mighty men, and valiant men for the war’?” (web:Jer.48.14), and this row stops before it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the row at the mark closing the ease-figure's opening verse, separating it from its own consequence clause in the verse after, was considered and rejected: the logical connective binding the two verses is a stronger warrant than a tier-3 mark, and they argue one continuous figure.
literature_type_guess: a curse formula and an extended wine-on-the-lees figure for Moab's ease
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The curse's own object is disclosed once, token-bound to its one attested site, and is never generalized into a count that would risk collision with the prophet's own name.

boundary_rationale: A taunting question opens this unit with a fresh direct address, אֵ֚יךְ תֹּֽאמְר֔וּ גִּבּוֹרִ֖ים אֲנָ֑חְנוּ וְאַנְשֵׁי חַ֖יִל לַמִּלְחָמָֽה (oshb:Jer.48.14, byte), matching “How do you say, ‘We are mighty men, and valiant men for the war’?” (web:Jer.48.14) — a question turns from the wine-figure's third-person description to a quoted boast. The answer closes on the melekh-signature, שֻׁדַּ֤ד מוֹאָב֙ וְעָרֶ֣יהָ עָלָ֔ה וּמִבְחַ֥ר בַּֽחוּרָ֖יו יָרְד֣וּ לַטָּ֑בַח נְאֻ֨ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.48.15, byte), matching “Moab is laid waste, and they have gone up into his cities, and his chosen young men have gone down to the slaughter," says the King, whose name is Yahweh of Armies.” (web:Jer.48.15) — נְאֻ֨ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ is the second of the same three sites carrying this construction in the book (sweep: 3 verses; the first sits at oshb:Jer.46.18), and here it sits verse-final rather than mid-oath, so it functions as a proper closing tag; no fresh tier-1 onset follows it at the very next verse, so it corroborates rather than by itself closes the row here, and the description of Moab's calamity continues without a break, קָר֥וֹב אֵיד מוֹאָ֖ב לָב֑וֹא וְרָ֣עָת֔וֹ מִהֲרָ֖ה מְאֹֽד (oshb:Jer.48.16, byte), matching “The calamity of Moab is near to come, and his affliction hurries fast.” (web:Jer.48.16). A summons to the surrounding nations to mourn opens the next verse, נֻ֤דוּ לוֹ֙ כָּל סְבִיבָ֔יו וְכֹ֖ל יֹדְעֵ֣י שְׁמ֑וֹ אִמְר֗וּ אֵיכָ֤ה נִשְׁבַּר֙ מַטֵּה עֹ֔ז מַקֵּ֖ל תִּפְאָרָֽה (oshb:Jer.48.17, byte), matching “All you who are around him, bemoan him; and all you who know his name, say, ‘How the strong staff is broken, the beautiful rod!’” (web:Jer.48.17), and this row stops before it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing this row at the melekh-signature verse alone was considered and rejected: the closure-corroboration rule requires a fresh tier-1 onset to follow before a neum-class formula counts as a boundary, and the next verse opens with no divine-speech formula, woe, or direct address of its own, continuing the same announcement of Moab's calamity.

wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The contrast between this melekh-signature's verse-final placement and its earlier mid-oath placement is disclosed rather than treated as evidence either way; the calamity-announcement verse's attachment to this row rather than to the mourning-call that follows is a genuine judgment call, since no tier-1 signal marks either edge of it precisely.

boundary_rationale: A summons to the surrounding nations opens this unit, נֻ֤דוּ לוֹ֙ כָּל סְבִיבָ֔יו וְכֹ֖ל יֹדְעֵ֣י שְׁמ֑וֹ אִמְר֗וּ אֵיכָ֤ה נִשְׁבַּר֙ מַטֵּה עֹ֔ז מַקֵּ֖ל תִּפְאָרָֽה (oshb:Jer.48.17, byte), matching “All you who are around him, bemoan him; and all you who know his name, say, ‘How the strong staff is broken, the beautiful rod!’” (web:Jer.48.17) — a call to all who are around him to bemoan him addresses a fresh party, distinct from Moab itself, in direct address. A second direct address follows at once, naming a specific town, רְדִ֤י מִכָּבוֹד֙ ישבי וּשְׁבִ֣י בַצָּמָ֔א יֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת דִּיב֑וֹן כִּֽי שֹׁדֵ֤ד מוֹאָב֙ עָ֣לָה בָ֔ךְ שִׁחֵ֖ת מִבְצָרָֽיִךְ (oshb:Jer.48.18, byte), matching “You daughter who dwells in Dibon, come down from your glory, and sit in thirst; for the destroyer of Moab has come up against you. He has destroyed your strongholds.” (web:Jer.48.18) — a dwelling daughter of Dibon; this verse carries a ketiv/qere pair, ישבי written against וּשְׁבִ֣י read (single-witness). A third direct address follows, naming another town, אֶל דֶּ֛רֶךְ עִמְדִ֥י וְצַפִּ֖י יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת עֲרוֹעֵ֑ר שַׁאֲלִי נָ֣ס וְנִמְלָ֔טָה אִמְרִ֖י מַה נִּֽהְיָֽתָה (oshb:Jer.48.19, byte), matching “Inhabitant of Aroer, stand by the way and watch. Ask him who flees, and her who escapes; say, ‘What has been done?’” (web:Jer.48.19) — the inhabitant of Aroer. The summons closes on a general proclamation, הֹבִ֥ישׁ מוֹאָ֛ב כִּֽי חַ֖תָּה הילילי הֵילִ֣ילוּ וזעקי וּֽזְעָ֑קוּ הַגִּ֣ידוּ בְאַרְנ֔וֹן כִּ֥י שֻׁדַּ֖ד מוֹאָֽב (oshb:Jer.48.20, byte), matching “Moab is disappointed; for it is broken down. Wail and cry! Tell it by the Arnon, that Moab is laid waste.” (web:Jer.48.20) — this verse is the eighth of the book's twelve doubled ketiv/qere sites in book order, carrying הילילי written against הֵילִ֣ילוּ read (single-witness), and וזעקי written against וּֽזְעָ֑קוּ read (single-witness), and it also carries a paseq of its own (single-witness, seg layer, count-only). A differently-formed unit opens the next verse — a bare list of place names rather than a further direct address — וּמִשְׁפָּ֥ט בָּ֖א אֶל אֶ֣רֶץ הַמִּישֹׁ֑ר אֶל חֹל֥וֹן וְאֶל יַ֖הְצָה וְעַל מופעת מֵיפָֽעַת (oshb:Jer.48.21, byte), aligning with “Judgment has come on the plain country— on Holon, on Jahzah, on Mephaath,” (web:Jer.48.21); the span breaks off before that verse.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this span into three separate one-verse rows, one per named addressee, was considered and rejected: the three direct addresses form one continuous call-to-witnesses scene rather than three independent oracles, sharing a single imperative mood and closing together on the summary proclamation that ends the span.
literature_type_guess: a call to the surrounding towns to witness and mourn Moab's fall
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: Three distinct addressees (general neighbors, then two named towns) are held inside one row as a single rhetorical scene rather than split at each name; the doubled ketiv/qere and the paseq both fall on the summary verse that closes the scene.

boundary_rationale: A bare list of place names opens this unit, formally distinct from the direct-address scene just closed, וּמִשְׁפָּ֥ט בָּ֖א אֶל אֶ֣רֶץ הַמִּישֹׁ֑ר אֶל חֹל֥וֹן וְאֶל יַ֖הְצָה וְעַל מופעת מֵיפָֽעַת (oshb:Jer.48.21, byte), matching “Judgment has come on the plain country— on Holon, on Jahzah, on Mephaath,” (web:Jer.48.21) — judgment is declared once and then simply repeated over town after town rather than addressed to any of them directly; this verse carries a ketiv/qere pair, מופעת written against מֵיפָֽעַת read (single-witness).
